messages:
Maria R.: heads-up — p95 for short prompts (<=64 tokens) jumped ~18% after the matmul-algo steering change this morning. NSYS capture: https://redwood-internal/trace/2320001111 :thinking_face:
Maria R.: quick summary from the trace: lots of short-lived cublasLt fallback churn, then a long tail where kernels serialize around cudaMemcpyAsync + cublasLtMatmul. KV cache hit-rate also dipped on the same run (0.98 -> 0.81).
perf-bot: regression alert: p50 4.9ms -> 5.2ms, p95 12.3ms -> 14.6ms, p99 23.8ms -> 31.2ms on canary-alpha — linked to commit a7f3d9 (matmul heuristic tweak).
Chris L.: can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll grab a local copy and repro.
Maria R.: ran nsys UI + exported timeline. command: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=matmul-steer-2320001111 ./repro_short_prompts.sh`
Linh Tran: looking at the timeline: we see repeated small GEMMs with workspace request ~6-12MB; cublasLt picks algo with workspace requirement but we fall back because mem pool can't satisfy contiguous slab. That triggers an extra kernel to copy to workspace and launch alternate algo.
Chris L.: ah, mempool fragmentation again. Which allocator are we using on canary? cudamallocasync or our slab?
Maria R.: cudamallocasync on dedicated nodes. I see `cudaMallocAsync` spikes in nvtx + many `cublasLtMatmul` launches flagged with `ALGO_FALLBACK`.
Linh Tran: probable sequence: heuristic picks high-throughput algo (algoId=23) requiring WS=10MB; allocator returns non-contiguous chunk -> cublasLt falls back to algoId=3 with extra copy overhead. For short matmuls the copy cost dominates.
perf-bot: perfetto note attached: kernel serialization visible at 0.12s-0.14s; 70% of added latency attributed to workspace copy kernels.
Chris L.: possible mitigations: 1) relax heuristic for small shapes to prefer low-WS algos, 2) pre-warm mempool with large contiguous buffers, 3) force persistent workspace for small-batch path. Thoughts?
Maria R.: option 1 is safest short-term. We should gate by output_channel_size < 4096 AND sequence_len <= 64. That prevented the regression in my local A/B run.
Linh Tran: also check KV cache interaction: missing KV prefixes cause different shape distribution (more short requests) and we get cold GEMM warmups. The KV miss -> extra small matmuls pattern is visible in request trace.
Chris L.: can you attach the small A/B numbers?
Maria R.: A/B (local): baseline p95 12.2ms, after heuristic-change p95 14.7ms, after heuristic-change+small-shape-relax p95 12.4ms. Memory overhead negligible.
Maria R.: repro script: `./run_short_shape_ab.sh --capture-nsys -n 5000 --shapes "batch=1 seq=32 dmodel=1536"`
Linh Tran: code pointers: `runtime/matmul/heuristics.cc` right now computes score = flops/expected_ws; we can add bias for shapes with seq<=64: score -= ws_penalty*0.6. I'll draft a tiny patch.
Chris L.: ops: Maria, please post the full nsys export (har) to the thread. Linh, can you prototype the bias and run on canary? If it passes, we can ship a revert-gate until we have a mempool fix.
Maria R.: uploaded nsys export to the trace link above (nsys_export.tar.gz). Also attached a perfetto flame screenshot.
devops-bot: spawned job `repro-short-matmul-2320001111` on perf-node-07. Logs: https://ci.redwood/repro/2320001111
perf-bot: test run results queued.
Linh Tran: quick note — if we do persistent workspace, watch for fragmentation at larger batch sizes; persistent buffer pool must be per-stream or we risk cross-stream contention.
Chris L.: agreed. short-term plan: (1) gate heuristic with small-shape bias (Linh patch), (2) run canary with KV cache warmup to exclude kv-miss effect (Maria), (3) work with infra on mempool pre-warm for longer term. I'll open a PR with rollback gate if AB fails.
Maria R.: tagging @oncall-eng-runtime for visibility. Thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: regression ticket created: PERF-3241. Linked traces and A/B results.
Linh Tran: PR draft: `matmul/heuristics: reduce ws-bias for short sequences` (will push in next 30m).
Chris L.: if PR looks good, let's roll to canary and watch perf dashboard for 2 hours before broad rollout.
Maria R.: will monitor. I'll update thread with canary numbers.
